decisions.question: Which commit-author trust model should the gateway use to distinguish own-role commits from pulled cross-role commits?

options.label: Lightweight: trust env-set git identity (coder@egg.local etc.) — read commit.author_email and key restrictions off it
Stronger: per-role GPG/SSH signing keys issued at sandbox start, gateway verifies signatures before honoring authorship
Hybrid: start with lightweight now, structure code so signing can be layered in later without a second rewrite
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: When a push contains ONLY blocked files (no allowed files), what should the gateway return?

options.label: Return 200 with nothing_to_push=true and list excluded files (matches 6f0877f50 behavior — silent soft-success; leaves blocked files uncommitted in worktree)
Return 200 with filtered=true and excluded files but surface a prominent warning in the response so agents notice
Return 403 (same as today) — all-blocked is a real policy violation, don't mask it with a 200
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Should auto-filtering be enabled by default or behind a feature flag?

options.label: Enabled by default (replace current 403 behavior outright). Flag EGG_AGENT_RESTRICTIONS_ENFORCE=false still disables the check entirely.
Enabled by default, but add a new EGG_AGENT_AUTOFILTER=false escape hatch to revert to 403-blocking behavior for debugging/rollback
Opt-in: default to current 403 behavior, enable auto-filter only when EGG_AGENT_AUTOFILTER=true (more conservative rollout)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: How should the gateway rewrite history when it needs to drop disallowed OWN-role commits from a push that also contains legitimate pulled cross-role commits?

options.label: Soft-reset + selective-commit (6f0877f50 style): reset to old_ref_sha, re-stage only allowed files from own work, re-commit with [auto-filtered] suffix. Loses the pulled commits entirely in this path — only safe when no pulled commits exist.

Interactive-rebase-equivalent: walk each own-role commit with git commit-tree/update-ref to rewrite it with blocked files removed, preserving pulled cross-role commits in between. More complex but handles mixed histories correctly.
Cherry-pick replay: reset to remote tip, replay pulled cross-role commits as-is, then replay own-role commits with blocked files dropped. Most robust but highest complexity.
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Should the pulled-commit pass-through trust the committer email, author email, or both?

options.label: Author email only (git log --pretty=%ae). The person who authored the content is what matters for role-scoping.
Committer email only (git log --pretty=%ce). The committer is who actually made the commit object in this repo.
Both must match a known egg role identity. Safest — a forged author with a non-egg committer gets rejected.
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: When the gateway auto-filters a push, what should happen to the agent's local HEAD after the gateway-side push completes?

options.label: Gateway leaves a filtered commit with [auto-filtered] suffix on the remote and restores the agent's original HEAD locally via git reset --hard (6f0877f50 behavior). Blocked files are left in worktree as uncommitted changes. The agent's local branch now DIVERGES from origin.
Gateway rewrites the agent's local HEAD to match what it pushed (fast-forward on origin). No divergence, but the blocked files are returned as uncommitted staged changes instead.
Gateway pushes filtered commit but also returns a mapping of (original_sha -> filtered_sha) in the response so the agent can realign itself if needed.
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: What happens to the client-side egg-orch push --scope-filter workaround once the gateway handles auto-filtering?

options.label: Keep it as a fallback — remains callable, useful for offline/manual rewriting, but agent-facing docs point to the gateway as primary
Deprecate with a warning — emit a message telling users the gateway handles this now, remove in a later release
Remove it entirely in this change — the gateway auto-filter fully supersedes it and keeping dead code adds maintenance burden
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Should auto-filter also apply to OTHER gateway checks that currently return 403 — phase-based file restrictions, anchor-write restrictions, protected-file restrictions?

options.label: Apply auto-filter consistently to all file-level push restrictions (phase, role, anchor, protected) — same rewrite pattern, most consistent agent experience
Apply auto-filter only to agent-role restrictions (minimal scope, matches #1470 original intent). Phase/anchor/protected stay 403 because they're more security-critical
Apply auto-filter to role AND phase restrictions but NOT to anchor/protected (those are harder security boundaries agents should never cross)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Which commit-authorship mechanism should the gateway trust to distinguish own vs pulled commits?

options.label: Author email from git log (lightweight, no new infra)
Per-role GPG/SSH signing keys (tamper-resistant, new infra)
Gateway-side commit-SHA registry (stateful, authoritative)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: How should the gateway auto-filter handle multi-commit own-authored pushes where some commits have blocked files?

options.label: Squash all own-authored commits into one with [auto-filtered] suffix (matches #1470)
Rewrite each commit individually, preserving commit structure
Reject multi-commit pushes when any file is blocked (force agent to squash first)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: What should the gateway do when ALL files in a push are blocked for the pushing role?

options.label: Return 200 with nothing_to_push=true, leave uncommitted changes in worktree (matches #1470)
Return 403 as before - there is nothing legitimate to push
Return 200 with nothing_to_push=true, preserve original commit in worktree HEAD (no rewrite)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Should the auto-filtered commit message include a [auto-filtered] suffix?

options.label: Yes - debugging breadcrumb, matches #1470
No - preserve original message verbatim, surface filter in response metadata only
Configurable via env var, default yes
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Should the push response include a pulled_commits field listing non-own-authored commits?

options.label: Yes - list of {sha, author} pairs for each pulled commit (transparency for agents + audit tooling)
No - keep response minimal, log pulled commits to audit log only
Only on filtered pushes (i.e. when auto-filter engaged)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: What is the rollout order for gateway auto-filter + author-exemption?

options.label: Enable both by default in the same release (recommended)
Ship in warn-only mode first, flip to enforce next release
Ship author-exemption standalone, leave auto-filter for a follow-up
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Where should the new partition-files-by-role helper live?

options.label: shared/egg_restrictions/checker.py (cross-component, reused by gateway and cli_push)
gateway/agent_restrictions.py (gateway-local, matches #1470 original location)
New module gateway/push_filter.py (separation-of-concerns)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Should the sandbox egg-orch push --scope-filter command be deprecated in the same PR?

options.label: Keep as-is (still useful outside gateway sessions)
Mark deprecated in --help, remove next release
Remove in the same PR (gateway now handles all cases)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Default behavior when a pulled commit's author email matches no known role?

options.label: Treat as own-commit, enforce restrictions (fail closed)
Treat as pulled commit, skip restrictions (fail open)
Block the push with a 403 (strict, suggests identity tampering)
Other (explain in reply)

questions.question: What attack model should drive the choice between author-email vs signed commits? Is there a documented threat where an agent forges another role's identity, or is the trust model 'the sandbox is the boundary' (so matching that for push authorship is acceptable)?

Should the gateway treat pulled commits authored by utility roles (e.g. conflict_resolver, autofixer) as exempt from the pushing role's file restrictions, the same as pulled commits from other execution roles?
If per-role signed commits are introduced later (future B2 option), is it acceptable that git reset --soft + git commit in the auto-filter path would drop signatures on the squashed commit?
Should the post_agent_commit hook run against the original pre-filter tip commit, or against the gateway-rewritten auto-filtered commit? Their semantics and audit trail differ.
Should the audit log distinguish 'auto-filtered' pushes from 'filtered due to pulled-commit exemption' pushes? They represent two different operational situations.
Are there roles whose file patterns we should explicitly exclude from the auto-filter path (e.g. autofixer, conflict_resolver given their cross-cutting scope), or should auto-filter apply uniformly?
What's the expected behavior when the gateway's rewrite collides with a server-side pre-push hook (e.g. branch protection rules that inspect commit message format)?
Should EGG_AGENT_FILE_PATTERNS (env var consumed by cli_push) be kept in lockstep with the gateway's source of truth, or is some duplication between the sandbox env and gateway patterns acceptable?
